title: He Told Her All His Heart
reflectionText: It was not the cords or the ropes that overcame him. It was words, pressed on him day after day, until his soul was troubled to death. Then he woke believing he would shake himself free as at other times, not knowing that Yahweh had departed. What is it that wears a strength down — not all at once, but a little every day, until it is gone?
editorialNotes: Text-First Story Factory 2.0 Batch A (journey backlog G4, approved 2026-07-22). Judges 16:4-22, absent both lanes. Fills the Samson-arc middle between existing 1142 (Judges 13, birth) and 1193 (Judges 16:23-31, death); VOICE_ARCHER shared with 1193 is a deliberate arc-continuity choice mirroring the 1564/1336 precedent. Boundary: ends at v22 (the hair beginning to grow again — the source's own seam into 1193) with no temple or death material and no forward-looking narration. SHORT + FULL (WEB 398w / 598w; KJV 440w / 509w). LONG omitted: the 19-verse source (~619 WEB words) has its honest ceiling inside the FULL band (same honest-ceiling finding as 1564 / 1 Samuel 24, ADR-030/031). Delilah's motive stated as the lords' silver only; Samson's torment carried by the source's own words ('his soul was troubled to death'); the cry 'The Philistines be upon thee, Samson!' kept from the source. SHORT compresses the three false answers into one movement. CODEX-AUDIT CORRECTION 2026-07-23 (Finding 3, accepted as full-source paraphrase). First remediation (commit 987e9c36) clustered the three tests and dropped reconstruction (run 41/89.2% -> 9/20.4%), but the re-audit judged the macro sequence still source-shaped and flagged a KJV-lane object mismatch ('loom' is the WEB rendering of v13; the KJV extract says 'the web' and 'the pin of the beam') plus an unsupported circumstance ('unregarded' at v22). SECOND REMEDIATION (this commit): the KJV FULL was re-authored again from a scene outline into four scene-based movements — the bargain and the three failed tests all folded into one movement (vv4-14); the wearing-down and the confession (vv15-17); the disclosure recognized and the shaving (vv18-19); the waking, the departed strength, the seizure, and the hair's regrowth (vv20-22). The WEB-derived 'loom' is replaced with KJV-grounded 'the web on the beam' and 'the pin'; 'unregarded' is removed; the v21 seizure sentence is restructured to break its source run. Sentence construction and scene granularity are rebuilt while canonical event chronology is preserved; the clause-by-clause cadence is not reproduced (this note makes no stronger claim than that). FINAL FIDELITY CORRECTION 2026-07-23 (second re-audit, 1574 new defects): (a) 'her hired men' was replaced with source-grounded 'men lay in wait in the chamber' — Judges 16:9 says men were lying in wait with her but not that she hired them; (b) the v21 sequence was corrected to eyes -> Gaza -> fetters -> grinding ('put out his eyes. They brought him down to Gaza, and there bound him with fetters of brass, and set him to grinding'), no longer implying he was in the fetters while being brought down. Current metrics (recomputed from the final file): run 9 (the factual seizure clause, v21) / coverage 43.5% / 509w (len(text.split())). The Nazarite confession and 'he wist not that the Lord was departed' are kept as essential lines. Per Finding 7, the figure-registry framing line was corrected from 'three times the ambush waited' to 'twice the hidden men waited in vain' — Judges 16 names men lying in wait only for the first two tests (16:9, 16:12); the KJV FULL likewise names the ambush only in rounds one and two. WEB short/full and KJV short unchanged.
